entities.observe: One flagstone sits a hair proud of its neighbors, the mortar cracked clean around its edge. Stepping square on it feels like a very bad idea.
entities.toast: The flagstone gives half an inch under your hand. Somewhere close, something CLICKS. Nothing else happens. This time.

entities._comment: Own graph (ksmvr_plates.json): the guide option is the real beat, gated on `horns_party_formed` (the party must exist to guide)
entities._comment_dig: 2026-07-27 Task 2.7 round 2 (controller-sanctioned): retires PERMANENTLY at horns_dig_joined. The delve-staging Horns had no present_when at all, so once round 1 fixed the inn-vs-camp bilocation the SAME bug relocated here -- during The Dig a player could meet camp-Ceria at the ruin and delve-hub-Ceria on the approach in one trip. No `_returned` twin on the delve maps, deliberately: the Horns moved on from the delve staging for good (the_horns_home already has them living at the inn; the dig and then the mounting is what brings them there). Safe for the seal beat -- this row is only gameplay-load-bearing during what_the_seal_kept, and seal_kept_reported gates the dig invitation, so horns_dig_joined cannot bank until that quest is done. Verified at QA level too: every script touching this map (delve_fight, delve_skill, delve_talk, dungeon_peek, dungeon_kingslayer_loop) runs on a fixture with horns_dig_joined absent, so no entity-count pin moves.

entities.skill_hint_toast: A narrow slit runs along the wall at knee height, primed and waiting. This wants a careful, deliberate touch, not a shove.
entities.locked_toast: A narrow slit runs along the wall at knee height. Whatever is loaded behind it, you have no idea how to disable it.
entities.item_hint_toast: A narrow slit runs along the wall at knee height, primed and waiting. Bare hands won't do it -- you'd want a proper kit for this.

on_skill_use.toast: You trace the mechanism with a careful eye, find the catch, and wedge it still with a wax-and-wire pick from the kit. The slit stays dark.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The floor ahead looks exactly like the floor behind you. Somehow, that is the part that bothers you.
entities.locked_toast: The floor ahead looks perfectly ordinary. Something about it still itches at the back of your mind.

on_skill_use.toast: You look again, and this time you see it: the grain runs the wrong way, and no dust has settled in months. That is not floor. That is a very good painting of floor.

entities.skill_hint_toast: Something under the stone hums off-key. Eyes that read mana could say what.
entities.locked_toast: The stone here looks like all the other stone. It is not.

on_skill_use.toast: [Detect Magic] — The seam lights up like a badly kept secret: old wardwork, still holding, drawn tight around the floor ahead. Now you know exactly what not to trust.

entities.observe: A coil of taut wire lies strung ankle-height between two stones, near-invisible against the dust. Whatever it is rigged to is worse than a stubbed toe.
entities.gate_closed_toast: You give the wire a wide berth. Something in the dark past it has not noticed you yet.

entities._comment: Matches rift_vermin_leak/ruin_guardian/awakened_boss's own interact-only convention for a boss the player consciously commits to, not an environmental ambush.
entities.observe: The hall ends in a sealed archway, and beyond it something vast fills the dark almost completely -- the same shape you glimpsed crouched near the entrance, closer now, utterly still. It is not still the way a statue is still.
entities.gate_closed_toast: Whatever waits beyond this arch, you are not walking into it yet — not with the halls still armed, not without the Horns at your back.

entities._comment: 2026-07-26 main-quest spec 7 amendment 1: display name was 'A Second Door'. The entity id is shipped and frozen; the fiction is not. This is a sealed rune-door full of wardwork by the hand that cut the inn's frame -- never a second Magical Door, never another portal. No QA script pins the old label (checked qa/scripts + qa/manifest).
entities.toast: The passage doesn't end here -- it just goes quiet, past a bend the light doesn't reach. Whatever's back there, this isn't the moment.
entities._comment_reading: 2026-07-26 Act V beat 2, THE READING (#270 beat 2). Three eyes on one door, the pantry-door consolidation idiom. LATER-SATISFIED-WINS across `variants` is what makes the bare interact a two-stage narration: with the descent agreed Pisces matches the hand (read_the_seal_runes), and once that is held his next read names the appetite (read_the_feeding_ward). That staging is DELIBERATE and load-bearing -- no main-line beat may sit behind a Skill the player's build might not own (spec 6's no-hard-gates rule applied to Skills), so the escort is the guaranteed producer of both reads and [Observe]/[Detect Magic] are the richer, earlier routes to the same facts. The pre-descent arms bank `sensed_something_deeper` (this prop's own shipped flavour counter) rather than the real reads, which ORDER-GATES the quest's beats: nothing in Act V can bank from a curious Act IV visit. The [Detect Magic] base arm deliberately does NOT bank `detected_wardwork` -- the quartet is the four shipped sites (inn frame, ruin socket, the seam back in these halls, the witch's hollow) and this door is what they drain INTO, not a fifth site; a fifth producer would also cheapen the >= 3 threshold its own payoff variant reads. SELF-REVIEW 2026-07-27: a `skill_hint_toast` authored here was DEAD COPY and is gone -- interactions.gd's prop branch reaches the requires_skill/hint arm only when there is no `on_interact_accomplishment`, and this prop has one. The pantry door's own comment names this class (inert copy dressed as a live surface); the hint a player actually gets is the bare interact's narration, which is the point of staging it. FIX ROUND 1 (reviewer CRITICAL, 2026-07-27): variants[0] is the repo's SOLE producer of `seal_kept_found`, and later-satisfied-wins meant the descent arm SHADOWED it -- a save that downed the construct but never touched this door (a pre-restructure save the Task 2.6 dig backfill carries into the pilgrimage is the reachable case) could descend, read, and never bank the find, which strands what_the_seal_kept's vault beat, then seal_kept_reported, then act_iv's own gate. Both Act V read arms now compound `seal_kept_found` into their gate (the :404 idiom): the skipped-find player banks the find on the first interact and the rune-read on the second, and every downstream read gate (read_the_seal_runes, and through it both [Detect Magic] variants) inherits the guarantee transitively. The [Observe] arm needed the SAME compound for the same reason -- it banks read_the_seal_runes without ever touching seal_kept_found, so gating it on the descent alone reopened the identical hole through a different arm. Regression-pinned in test_sim_core (_test_seal_door_find_before_read).

variants.toast: The runes are the same. Not similar — the same hand, the same order, as the door in the inn's pantry.
Pisces reaches the door before you do and stops a handspan short of it. "The same hand. Not a school, not a fashion. A HAND, and it cut this one first." He does not look away while he says it.

Pisces steps back at last. "It is not a lock. The lines run one way, they have run one way for a very long time, and something on the far side has been drinking the whole while. Your inn has a frame by this hand. Sleep well."
The runes keep their slow one-way order. Pisces has stopped narrating and started counting under his breath, which is worse.

observe.toast: [Observe] — Worked stone, deliberate, and not one line of it reads like a lock. Whatever this door is for, it is not keeping people out. You would have to stand here longer, with someone who knows more than you do.

variants.toast: [Observe] — You take the runes in order, the way you would read a sentence. The turns repeat at a fixed interval. The pantry frame does exactly that, at exactly that interval, and this one is worn deeper: it has been doing it longer. Behind you, Pisces says nothing, which from him is applause.

detect_magic.toast: [Detect Magic] — Wardwork, and awake. It does not flare and settle the way a bound ward should. It holds one low steady note, like a breath nobody has to let out, and you have felt that note somewhere else.

variants.toast: [Detect Magic] — The ward opens under your sight and does not stop opening. It is not holding anything shut. It is POURING: one direction, one slow measured rate, into whatever the stone is between. It has poured since before the city. Pisces, very quietly: "Ah. So that is what the others were."

[Detect Magic] — Every reading you have taken lines up at once: the inn's frame, the ruin's socket, the seam back down the hall, the hollow west of Riverfarm. Not four wards. One lattice, and this door is where it drains to. Something behind this stone has been drinking Liscor's oldest work since before Liscor. Pisces uses a word you have never heard him use in public.

entities._comment_door: 2026-07-26 Act V beat 3, the FIGHT path. door_when is checked BEFORE the interact arm (interactions.gd prop branch order), so once seal_opened banks this stops being a thing to read and becomes a way through -- which is exactly the fiction. seal_opened banks ONLY on Pisces' open-it fork, so the TALK and SKILL paths leave this door shut forever, as #270 requires.

door_when.open_toast: The seal does not resist. It simply stops being a seal — the runes go quiet in order, one ring at a time, and the door swings in on three centuries of undisturbed air.

entities._comment: 2026-07-26 Act V: THE SEAL'S WARDEN. present_when is validator-forbidden on encounters, so it stands here from first arrival, VISIBLE AND INERT (the rift_vermin_leak pattern) with its own observe + gate_closed_toast -- a shape in the alcove the player has walked past since the delve, which is the whole point when it finally moves. encounter_when arms it on seal_opened alone: it wakes because the seal broke, and only the FIGHT fork breaks it. trigger_radius 1 makes it UNSKIPPABLE on that fork without paying for it -- (18,7) is the only walkable approach to the door, and it sits one cell off. A sneaking player still slips by and banks sneaked_past_danger, the shipped stealth reward, which is a real build paying a real price rather than an oversight. CELL (19,6): the pocket north of the door, reachable only from (19,5), so it blocks no route -- and it is NOT (18,7), which delve_fight stands on. Roster: `seal_warden`, a distinct id per combatants.json:401.
entities._comment_victory: on_victory is the ENGINE DEFAULT spelled out (test_combat_data requires the key present on every encounter): the warden banks no story counter of its own. Act V's resolution belongs to the room behind it -- vault_anchor_stone's open is what banks seal_resolved -- so a player who sneaks past the fight and one who flattens it reach the same beat by different costs.
entities.gate_closed_toast: Dust lies on it in an unbroken sheet, the way dust lies on a thing that has not moved in centuries. Leave it that way.
entities.observe: An alcove beside the sealed door, and something standing in it: ward-stone, shoulder-high, cut in the same hand as the runes. It is not a statue. Statues are not built facing the door they guard.
entities._comment_loot: DELIBERATELY no `loot` array. Every enchanted accessory this fight could plausibly drop (warded_coil_charm, construct_core_shard, guardian_ward_fragment) is a chance-1.0 drop from a fight the player must already have won to be standing here, and `pickup` no-ops a duplicate id -- a guaranteed-dead drop reads worse than none. The reward for this fight is the room behind it (seal_anchor_rune) plus the quest's own resolution_paths grant.

entities._comment: 2026-07-26 Act V: THE ESCORT. Pisces is the voice at this door -- the prop never speaks (Global Constraint), so his narration rides the prop's toasts and everything that needs OPTIONS lives here. present_when brackets from the descent ask onward and never closes: after the resolution he is still the man standing in front of the thing he spent a month on, and a vanished escort would read as a bug. CELL (19,8): deliberately NOT (18,7), which is delve_fight's own standing cell for the seal_kept_found beat -- an entity there would strand a shipped canonical mid-route. Open neighbours (18,8)/(19,9), and no shipped save can hold seal_descent_agreed at all, so the new blocker can strand nothing. Bilocation with the Guild-steps Pisces is the shipped pisces_mounting precedent (Task 2.4): different maps, never on screen together.
entities.observe: He has not sat down since you got here. One hand hovers a finger's width off the stone, tracking something along it that nobody else in the hall can see, and his lips move without sound.

dialogue.speaker: Pisces
dialogue.text: Quietly, if you can manage it. I have lost the count twice already and blamed you both times.

entities._comment: respawns:true (dormant until the next sleep, the rock_crab_nest/kingslayer_den mechanism).
entities.gate_closed_toast: Rubble and old wardwork still choke this side passage. Whatever's back there can wait until the main halls are actually safe.
entities.observe: A narrower passage breaks off from the gauntlet proper, half-choked with fallen stone. Small shapes move in the dark past the rubble -- more than one.

companion_source.taken_toast: The bones rise and fall into step behind you.

entities.observe: Old bones, settled where they fell. They are not going anywhere. Probably.
